correctness.rationale: The finite three-layer frame has root r, one nonreflexive world per nonempty k-uniform hyperedge and reflexive singleton-access worlds for vertices. At a leaf world, Box Diamond p and Diamond Box p agree; at each nonempty edge-world, if the premise holds then all its leaves satisfy p and hence the conclusion holds. At root failure means all hyperedges have a p-vertex but none lies entirely in p, i.e. a two-colouring with every edge bichromatic, including the empty edge-family convention (then r itself refutes the axiom). At rank one, any nonempty edge forbids such colouring, exactly FO-definable nonemptiness. Rank two is graph non-bipartiteness/odd cycle, decidable in L via parity double-cover undirected reachability and Reingold. L-hardness: subdivide each input USTCON edge to make bipartite S(G), add edge st; an odd cycle exists exactly when s,t were connected, and the tuple-based local construction is first-order interpretable on ordered encodings. Rank-three complement is 3-uniform hypergraph two-colourability (monotone NAE-3SAT), NP-complete, giving coNP-completeness. The original source verify_mckinsey_rank.py was read; a separate direct full-valuation evaluator checked root and all other worlds on 30 rank-one, 74 rank-two and 18 rank-three finite hypergraphs, each agreeing with bicolourability. These finite checks do not prove space/class hardness; no L != coNP separation is claimed. FO-completeness assumes standard fixed-arity tuple input encodings and the known stronger completeness of USTCON under first-order interpretations.

value.rationale: The rank-one/rank-two/rank-three break identifies a sharp definability/logspace/coNP computational boundary in a motivated natural subclass of modal frames. It is a nontrivial structural transfer from hypergraph edge size to modal validity complexity, with explicit first-order hardness at rank two. It avoids claiming complexity-class separation or pretending the known general coNP theorem and odd-cycle lemma are new.
